description:
PROBLEM
Failover correctness for the whole system hinges on the coordinator's own durability, and that authority is still an open decision: ADR-004/TD-002 leave the durable metadata home undecided between object-log internal topics (primary candidate) and Postgres (fallback), behind the pluggable CoordinatorStore (ADR-008; crates/fjord-coordinator/src/{memory.rs,postgres.rs}). Brokers are stateless by design, so the coordinator is the only stateful component whose loss story matters — leaving its durability authority undecided blocks any honest production-failover claim.

CURRENT STATE
- MemoryCoordinator (non-durable, dev/test) and PgCoordinator (durable via Postgres transactions, per-partition FOR UPDATE row locks in postgres.rs:323-524) exist.
- No object-log-internal-topics coordinator implementation exists.
- The produce ack floor is object PUT + coordinator commit, so the decision also bounds produce latency (a slower durable substrate cannot be hidden).

PROPOSED FIX
Write the deciding ADR: evaluate object-log internal topics vs Postgres as the durable coordinator authority against (a) commit latency on the produce path, (b) recovery/failover of the coordinator itself (who replays what, from where, with what fencing), (c) operational surface (the no-hosted-control-plane thesis in ADR-006 favors fewer stateful dependencies), (d) the SPIKE-001 measurement plan (still unrun — either run it as part of this decision or record why it can be deferred). Record the decision, the rejected alternative with rationale, and the migration/compatibility implications for existing PgCoordinator deployments. Derive follow-up implementation beads in the ADR but do not file them (operator review first).

NON-SCOPE
- No coordinator implementation work in this bead; decision and ADR only.
- No change to the CoordinatorStore trait surface unless the decision requires documenting a needed extension.
title: Decide and record the durable coordinator-metadata authority (object-log internal topics vs Postgres)

3. compaction_index_switch_is_atomic: concurrent fetches during compaction never observe a gap or duplicate — every offset resolves to exactly one of (old L0, new L1).
4. compaction_marks_superseded_l0_dead: superseded L0 objects become reclaimable; live branches of the index never reference them post-switch.

description:
PROBLEM
Compaction is declared mandatory (ADR-005 section 6) and PRD durability/scale requirement D9 tests for it, but it does not exist: BackendCapabilities.compaction = false (crates/fjord-heimq-backend/src/lib.rs:347; crates/fjord-broker/src/lib.rs:317) and a repo grep for compact/L1 finds only test fixtures. Consequences accumulate unbounded: every flush multiplexes many (topic,partition) batches into one small L0 object keyed seg/{host}-{pid}-{counter}-{nanos} (fjord-heimq-backend/src/lib.rs:222-232), so historical fetch does one object GET per tiny L0 object and coordinator index rows grow without bound — the exact failure mode D9 exists to catch.

CURRENT STATE
- Objects are flat L0 only; no offset-sorted rewrite exists.
- The reclamation seams are already sketched: truncate_before advances log_start and drops index rows (crates/fjord-coordinator/src/postgres.rs:652-671); dead-object handling at sequencer.rs:204-216 and object-log engine.rs:340-350.
- TD-005 section Compaction and ADR-005 section 6 specify the intended design: background rewrite of L0 objects into offset-sorted L1 objects per (topic,partition) range, with the coordinator index switch as the atomic commit point (readers resolve via index_lookup, so switching index entries from L0 to L1 ranges re-routes fetches without a read-path change).

PROPOSED FIX
Implement the TD-005 design: a background compaction task (fjord broker/server side) that (1) selects L0 object ranges per partition past a size/age threshold, (2) reads and rewrites them into offset-sorted L1 objects, (3) commits by atomically replacing the covered fjord_index entries with the L1 entries in one coordinator transaction (the index switch is the commit point; concurrent fetches see either old L0 or new L1 entries, never a gap), (4) marks superseded L0 objects dead for reclamation via the existing dead-object seam. Set BackendCapabilities.compaction = true when the capability is real. Config: thresholds, concurrency, enable/disable.

NON-SCOPE
- Key-based Kafka log compaction (cleanup.policy=compact semantics) — this is size/layout compaction only.
- Object reclamation policy changes beyond marking superseded L0 objects dead.
- Read caching (separate bead).
title: Implement L0-to-L1 offset-sorted compaction with index switch

acceptance:
1. cargo test passes.

3. Either the test demonstrates existing sequencer-side fencing suffices (documented with the test name in the architecture/failover doc), or the minimal coordinator-side fencing fix is applied and covered by the same test.

description:
PROBLEM
Broker failover is a routing-only event (reassign_leader + leader_epoch bump, crates/fjord-broker/src/lib.rs:115-122), and the append path does not fence on broker epoch: the backend receives the leader epoch but ignores it (crates/fjord-heimq-backend/src/lib.rs:591 takes _leader_epoch unused; append at lib.rs:443 proceeds regardless). This is defensible only if single-writer ordering and stale-writer rejection genuinely rest on the sharded single-writer sequencer (ADR-007; crates/fjord-coordinator/src/sequencer.rs) — i.e., two brokers concurrently accepting produces for the same partition after a leadership change cannot corrupt ordering, duplicate offsets, or violate idempotency/EOS guarantees. That claim is currently an architecture assertion without direct test evidence.

CURRENT STATE
- leader_epoch is tracked and surfaced in Metadata responses for client routing only.
- The coordinator commit path (PgCoordinator.commit_object, crates/fjord-coordinator/src/postgres.rs:323-524) takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE per partition row and runs idempotency/epoch checks — this is where stale-writer safety should hold.
- No test currently exercises concurrent produce through two broker instances across a reassign_leader event.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a regression that runs two broker instances against one coordinator, drives reassign_leader mid-stream, and produces concurrently to the same partition from both; assert offsets remain contiguous and gap-free, no duplicate offsets, idempotent-producer dedup holds, and consumers see a single consistent order. If the test exposes a window where a stale broker's commit is accepted incorrectly, add the minimal fencing (e.g., coordinator-side epoch check on commit) — do not add broker-side WAL/lease machinery. Document the outcome in the failover section of the architecture docs: either "sequencer provides fencing, evidence: <test>" or the fix applied.

NON-SCOPE
- No broker-side durable state, lease store, or WAL recovery machinery (brokers stay stateless per ADR-005).
- No changes to client-visible Metadata/leader semantics.
title: Prove split-brain write safety rests on the sequencer; add fencing evidence for the unfenced append path

description:
<context-digest>
<principles>HELIX is the normative design; local cache is never authoritative; immutable object bytes permit safe read caching</principles>
<concerns>object-store GET cost | tail latency | concurrent cache misses</concerns>
<practices>Instrumented BlobStore tests | parity suite | public capability manifest</practices>
<adrs>TD-006 Fetch read path and locality-aware cache; PRD FR-29</adrs>
<governing>TD-006 requires an aligned chunk cache with single-flight and cache-loss correctness.</governing>
</context-digest>

PROBLEM
Every v0.1.3 fetch reads object storage directly: object-log performs index_lookup and get_range with no Fjord chunk cache, single-flight dedup, or hot-tail serving. Repeated consumers multiply GET cost, and FR-29 cache metrics cannot exist while no cache is present.

IMPLEMENTATION
Add a CachingBlobStore decorator around the configured store before engine construction: aligned, size-bounded LRU chunks keyed by object and chunk index; single-flight dedup for concurrent misses; hit, miss, and dedup metrics; configuration for chunk size, capacity, and enablement. Keep cache contents non-authoritative. If serving un-PUT tail data requires upstream object-log work, capture that gap as a follow-on bead rather than editing HELIX. Update docs/public/data/capabilities.json when release evidence exists. HELIX artifacts are read-only for this implementation bead.

NON-SCOPE
Distributed cache ownership; compaction; changes to TD-006 or other HELIX artifacts.
title: Add tiered read cache: chunk LRU BlobStore decorator with single-flight (TD-006)

PROBLEM
v0.1.3 packages the Helm chart only as an expiring GitHub Actions artifact. The release does not publish the chart to a durable repository, and no release gate pulls the published chart and image by tag into kind. A rendered local chart therefore does not prove that an external operator can install matching release artifacts.

IMPLEMENTATION
Publish each tagged chart as a versioned OCI artifact under the repository owner in GHCR, with chart version and appVersion derived from the tag. Add a release verification job that anonymously pulls the published chart and image, installs them into kind using the release tag, waits for readiness, and runs a standard Kafka-client produce/consume smoke. Record chart digest, image digest, release tag, and commands as workflow evidence. Keep HELIX artifacts read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Custom domains; a hosted control plane; edits to HELIX design artifacts.

description:
<context-digest>
<principles>HELIX is the normative design; brokers are stateless; group generation and committed offsets belong in the central coordinator</principles>
<concerns>Kafka group state machine | restart durability | multi-broker coordinator routing</concerns>
<practices>Standard-client restart tests | Postgres conformance | capability-gated ApiVersions</practices>
<adrs>TD-007 consumer-group coordinator; COORD-001 group-state contract; API-001 group API surface</adrs>
<governing>TD-007 and COORD-001 require group membership, assignments, generations, and offsets to live in CoordinatorStore and survive broker loss.</governing>
</context-digest>

PROBLEM
v0.1.3 persists OffsetCommit/OffsetFetch through CoordinatorOffsetStore, but the running Server::with_backends_and_cluster_view constructs Heimq ConsumerGroupManager for JoinGroup/SyncGroup/Heartbeat/LeaveGroup. FjordGroupCoordinator is process-local, reports durability None, is not backed by CoordinatorStore, and is not injected into the binary. A broker restart therefore loses active group membership, generation, and assignment state even with Postgres configured.

IMPLEMENTATION
Add or extend the Heimq server injection seam so Fjord supplies a GroupCoordinatorBackend backed by the same CoordinatorStore used for sequencing and offsets. Implement the classic group state transitions, generation fencing, assignments, heartbeats/session expiry, and multi-broker FindCoordinator routing against that durable authority. Capability-gate group APIs until this backend is installed. Update docs/public/data/capabilities.json from release evidence. HELIX artifacts are read-only.

NON-SCOPE
KIP-848 next-generation groups; edits to HELIX design artifacts.
title: Wire durable consumer-group state through CoordinatorStore

description:
<context-digest>
<principles>HELIX is the normative design; acknowledged offsets require sequencing; public release claims require executable evidence</principles>
<concerns>Kafka ack semantics | object-log durability boundary | fetch visibility</concerns>
<practices>Boundary tests for acks=0/1/all | standard-client parity | public capability manifest</practices>
<adrs>API-001 Kafka compatibility surface; TD-003 object-log data plane</adrs>
<governing>API-001 maps acks=1 to Fjord durable commit by default, allows rejection by profile, and permits acks=0 without a durability claim.</governing>
</context-digest>

PROBLEM
The v0.1.3 produce backend hardcodes Ack::Sequenced for every client request. The Heimq handler suppresses the acks=0 response but still waits for the same sequencing path, and the backend never receives the client ack value. This does not implement the distinct API-001 acks=0 behavior and leaves the release unable to evidence all three ack modes.

IMPLEMENTATION
Thread the client acks value through the Heimq/Fjord backend seam. Keep acks=1 and acks=all at Fjord durable sequencing as designed; make acks=0 fire-and-forget without exposing uncommitted data. Record the implemented release behavior in docs/public/data/capabilities.json and generated public compatibility documentation. HELIX artifacts are read-only for this implementation bead.

NON-SCOPE
Changing the API-001 ack mapping; weakening acks=1 below durable sequencing; changing consumer visibility.
title: Map client Kafka acks to object-log Ack level in the produce path
